chunks: From him, from Salamah, from al-Hasan ibn Yusuf, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever is born upon the natural disposition (fitrah) and is known for righteousness in his own self, his testimony is valid.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Natural disposition or innate inclination towards good

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a witness's testimony to be valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) highlights the jurisprudential principle that innate moral disposition (*fitrah*) serves as a reliable indicator of a witness's integrity (*adalah*). It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on internal righteousness as a prerequisite for legal testimony, linking personal piety directly to judicial validity.
